data.narrative: Completed Module 1 AI Engineering Mindset - chose task-by-task delegation strategy for unfamiliar codebase and complex feature. Created starter workspace, generated architecture summary and extension points analysis through AI agent. Performed trust audit with verification commands (ls src, cat models, cat routes). Found discrepancy: agent accurately described created Node.js starter workspace, but actual CAW Assessment project uses Python FastAPI with PostgreSQL. Root cause identified as insufficient context - created wrong workspace instead of using existing application. Created corrected architecture summary. Learned that AI generates and human decides - trust-but-verify workflow critical.

dimension_scores.observation: Wrote specific prompts for architecture summary (folder structure, data models, API routes, auth, database) and extension points analysis (routes location, models location, middleware pattern, background jobs). Prompts were constrained and specific, not vague 'summarize this codebase'.
dimension_scores.evidence: architecture-summary-prompt.md: 'Summarize the architecture of this project. Include: (1) folder structure with one-sentence description of each top-level directory, (2) all data models with their fields and relationships, (3) every API route with its HTTP method and purpose, (4) how authentication works, (5) the database technology and how connections are configured.'

dimension_scores.observation: Performed trust audit with three verification commands (ls src, cat src/models/store.js, cat src/routes/index.js). Verified factual claims against actual files. Discovered discrepancy when comparing to parent project - agent described starter workspace accurately but actual project uses different stack. Documented discrepancy in trust-audit.md with corrected summary and root cause analysis.
dimension_scores.evidence: trust-audit.md: 'Verification Commands Run: ls src, cat src/models/store.js, cat src/routes/index.js. BREAK: Discrepancy Found - Agent's claim about in-memory storage vs actual PostgreSQL with SQLAlchemy ORM.'

dimension_scores.observation: Caught workspace error in BREAK step after one verification cycle. Created corrected architecture summary instead of re-prompting agent. Identified root cause as insufficient context issue (fixable with better prompts) rather than ambiguous code or hallucination. Documented lesson learned for future modules.
dimension_scores.evidence: trust-audit.md: 'Why the Agent Got It Wrong: Cause: Insufficient context. Lesson learned: always check for existing application directories before creating starter workspace.'

dimension_scores.observation: Chose task-by-task delegation strategy over full autopilot for unfamiliar codebase and complex multi-part feature. Reasoning: wrong assumptions cascade silently through all subsequent work. Task-by-task catches errors after 30 lines instead of discovering after 500 lines. Recognized that this is the same tradeoff real engineering leads face when managing human teams.
dimension_scores.evidence: Decision: 'Delegation strategy: Task-by-Task. Codebase is unfamiliar - team collaboration product with role-based permissions, invites, activity feed, audit log. Wrong assumption early would cascade through all subsequent work.'

dimension_scores.observation: Produced verified understanding of codebase architecture with documented trust audit. Created corrected architecture summary that accurately describes actual CAW Assessment project (Python FastAPI, PostgreSQL with SQLAlchemy ORM, Redis caching, Celery background tasks). All verification commands passed for starter workspace claims. Discrepancy documented with root cause and lesson learned.
dimension_scores.evidence: architecture-summary-corrected.md: 'Python FastAPI framework, PostgreSQL database with SQLAlchemy ORM, Redis for caching, Celery for background tasks, Pydantic for configuration validation'

strengths: Chose task-by-task delegation strategy for unfamiliar codebase with clear reasoning about error cascading
Performed targeted verification commands to validate agent's factual claims
Identified root cause of discrepancy (insufficient context) and documented lesson learned
Created corrected architecture summary based on actual project structure
data.recommendation: Module 1 complete. Ready for Module 2 - Decompose Team Collaboration feature into executable tasks.

public_evidence.ability: AI-augmented engineering - trust-but-verify workflow for validating agent outputs
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates critical AI engineering skill - verifying AI agent outputs through independent commands, identifying discrepancies, understanding root causes (insufficient context vs hallucination vs ambiguous code), and applying lessons learned to future work. This is essential for using AI safely in production.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Reflection: 'The solution is a trust-but-verify workflow: get the agent's output, pause to assess what you trust vs what needs verification, run targeted verification commands, and document discrepancies.'

concepts_demonstrated.concept: The AI generates, the human decides
concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Reflection: 'The module solves the problem of trusting AI agent outputs without verification. The core problem is that AI agents can hallucinate or make assumptions based on typical patterns rather than actual codebase realities.'

Reflection: 'AI gets you 80% of the way in 20% of time (scaffold, boilerplate, straightforward logic). The remaining 20% (review, edge cases, security, integration) takes 80% of effort - that's where engineering skill lives.'

learning_style_signals: values verification over trust in AI outputs
prioritizes understanding root causes of errors
